body:
I won't be able to make the call, but here is my proposal for how to adapt the fork rollout process: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/1715 

I'll send it to various L2s, LSTs and infra providers today for them to comment on it.

I've prepared a list of bugs client teams have reported from the last non finality test on devnet 3 (list is not complete yet):
https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/fusaka-syncing-bugs

> * [Protocol Upgrade Process](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md) and testnets

i really think that having 3 months of a potential 6 month cycle as the road to mainnet is not practical.
 - 30 days between client release (we'd previously said last testnet going live) and mainnet date
 - 30 days between client release and first testnet going live
 - at least 2 weeks between testnets (hoodi, sepolia) in future i guess, basically another 30 days

This would leave maybe 3 months to do all the development cycles and get ready for testnet, finding bugs, merging, etc etc if we want everyone to be on master before first testnet.

Something has to give. If we want this release timeframe, then I don't see how we can maintain a 6 month cadence as well.
@rolfyone there is a suggestion to make the timelines a bit more compact: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/1715

Agree with @rolfyone, no way we can maintain 6 month fork cadence. It just isn't possible with the rollout strategy. However I don't think we can adjust the rollout strategy much - we obviously aren't going to reduce it to 1 month. Too many people and companies depend on Ethereum and need to actively prepare for the fork.
